subject: Close plan: performance MAP + surge vs sustain benchmarking
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@astrahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Weaver <tom.weaver@strata.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Performance MAP and close timeline - initial ask

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Astra is excited about Redwood's unified runtime — before we greenlight the pilot we need a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes a concrete performance evaluation and a proposed close timeline. High-level asks from our side:

- Target latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 250ms for our typical prompts (avg ~280 tokens).
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) requirement for chat flows: < 150ms median.
- Sustained throughput: support 800 concurrent chat sessions for peak hours; ability to tolerate bursts up to 2,500 concurrent sessions for short periods (5-10 min).
- We care about queueing/backpressure behavior — we cannot have request timeouts during bursts.

I attached our workload profile (astra_workload_profile_v1.pdf). Can you map out an evaluation plan (test matrix + metrics) and a proposed MAP with milestones and an expected close date? Procurment will want a simple canary/rollback plan and an estimate for committed capacity pricing.

Best,
Linda
Director, Platform Engineering
Astra Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Linda Park <linda@astrahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:37:00-05:00
Subject: Proposed evaluation plan (test matrix + metrics)

Hi all — drafting the evaluation plan below (attached as redwood_performance_test_plan.md). TL;DR: we run 3 phases (baseline, burst stress, steady-state) across two model variants (rwd-bert-arch-v2, rwd-llama-quant) and collect latency distribution, TTFT, throughput (tokens/sec), queue depth, error rates, and system resource metrics.

Test matrix (summary):
- Workloads: 3 prompt templates from Astra doc (control, clinical-summary, triage-chat). Avg tokens: 280, 420, 160.
- Concurrency steps: 100, 400, 800, 1,500, 2,500 (each step = N concurrent sessions holding streaming connections).
- Ramp pattern: 10m linear ramp to target, sustain 10m (steady-state run), then cool-down. Burst scenario: 1m linear ramp to target, sustain 5-10m, then backoff. Repeat 3 iterations.
- KV cache states: cold vs warmed (we'll run warmed runs after a 15-min warm-up).

Metrics captured:
- TTFT (ms): time from request accepted to first token sent.
- Latency (ms): p50/p90/p95/p99 for full-response completion.
- Throughput: tokens/sec aggregated and per-worker.
- Queueing: average & max queue length, time-in-queue histograms.
- Error rate: 4xx/5xx, retry counts, circuit-open events.
- Resource: GPU util, memory, I/O, and host-level throttles.

Acceptance criteria (suggested MAP gates):
- Steady-state (800 concurrency): p95 latency <= 250ms, TTFT median <= 150ms, error rate < 0.5%.
- Burst tolerance (2,500 concurrency for 5m): no more than 10% p95 latency degradation vs steady-state and queuing should not cause request timeouts; system should auto-fallback to a compatible smaller model if saturation hits >85% GPU util.

Operational knobs to tune during tests:
- Request-level rate limits (requests/sec per API key) and token-level throttles.
- Per-customer token-bucketing and short-window burst allowance.
- Autoscale trigger: GPU pool scale when avg queue depth > X for Y seconds.

Attachments: redwood_performance_test_plan.md (test scripts, prometheus dashboards, artifact locations). I'll start the infra runs tomorrow if we get sign-off from Astra.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@astrahealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T15:46:00-05:00
Subject: MAP + results summary (pilot runs completed)

Team — we ran the evaluation per the plan between 2026-12-02 and 2026-12-05 (runs executed in US-east and EU regions to validate routing). Attached: map-20261206-results-summary.csv and a short PDF with charts (rate-limit-recommendation.pdf). Summary of key findings and MAP milestones below.

Executive summary (short):
- Steady-state (800 concurrent, warmed cache) — rwd-llama-quant met Astra's steady criteria: TTFT median = 85ms, p95 completion latency = 210ms, error rate = 0.12%. Aggregate throughput = ~45k tokens/sec.
- Burst (2,500 concurrent, 5–10m sustain) — we observed queueing spikes: p95 completion latency increased to 430ms on the slower model; rwd-bert-arch-v2 exhibited p95 = 520ms and saw transient 4xx retry events when queue depth exceeded configured host queue limit.
- Cold-cache runs increased TTFT by ~60–85ms across templates; recommending a warm-up policy for sustained peaks.
- Observed a soft-failure mode where request-level rate limiting prevented full queue growth but caused elevated 429s for aggressive multi-request clients.

Recommendations for MAP and close plan:
1) Rate-limit tuning: implement a two-tier limit — per-key sustained RPS and a short-window burst allowance. Suggested values: sustained RPS = 20 req/sec per API key, short-window burst = 200 req in 60s per key (token-aware). These produced safe tail latencies during our run. See attached rate-limit-recommendation.pdf for the tuning curves.
2) Autoscale + warm-up: enable an autoscale threshold at avg queue depth > 120 for 30s, and perform a pre-warm of model KV cache 15 minutes prior to predicted peak windows.
3) Canary cadence: 1-week canary with 10% traffic, monitor TTFT and p95 latency, abort criteria = p95 latency > 30% above pilot steady-state for 3 consecutive 5-min windows.
4) Fallback policy: prefer rwd-llama-quant as the default for Astra (best steady performance); configure fallback to rwd-bert-arch-v2 for lower cost during non-critical windows with throttled concurrency.
5) Procurement: recommend Reserved Capacity plan for steady 800 concurrency with burst buffer for additional 1,800 concurrent sessions billed on burst usage.

Next steps / MAP milestones (dates are target):
- 2026-12-07: Redwood sends final MAP doc + signed test artifacts to Astra (this thread).
- 2026-12-09: Astra signs pilot PO (DocuSign link in related_links).
- 2026-12-13 — 2026-12-19: Canary week (10% traffic).
- 2026-12-20: Final billing/commit sign-off if canary gates passed.

Linda — please confirm the PO cadence and compliance retention window you need for audit logs (we support 90/365 day retention; we can extend to 730 on request but need procurement sign-off).

Attachments referenced: map-20261206-results-summary.csv (raw metrics), rate-limit-recommendation.pdf, redwood_performance_test_plan.md (test harness).

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
